Name: Can The Player Leave - Out of Bounds Checker
Author: pneuma163
Description:
[size=3]This mod is primarily for map makers, whether you are making a new greenhouse, a map patch, or an entire new collection of maps in an expansion.

This mod adds a command "escapemap" to be used in the SMAPI console. This mod has no in game UI or effect. There are three main arguments that can be provided in any order, though there are some restrictions.

Here's the output of "help escapemap" in the console for more details:[/size]

[code]﻿escapemap: Prints out the locations where a player can leave a map.
- Optional arguments in any order:
    "print" (or "grid") - prints a "graphical" grid of the location(s) requested.
    "any" (or "all") - includes any map currently loaded, excluding the farmhouse. By default only the current map is considered.
    "farmhouse" - USED ALONE - prints a "graphical" grid of the farmhouse with no further information.
For example "escapemap any grid" prints information as well as the grid of all currently loaded locations, excluding the farmhouse.
            "escapemap farmhouse any grid" only prints the farmhouse grid.
            "escapemap" prints only text information (no grid) for the current location.
In vanilla 1.6.8, "escapemap" mentions the Backwoods, Summit, and possibly Town (community upgrade depending).
[/code]
[size=4][b]Important notes:[/b][/size][size=3]

- This mod only considers locations it thinks that a player could walk or otherwise warp to. For example, it will likely not test your mod's brand new map unless the map has warps set up or you warp the player there and then run the command. For the sake of an example, it will however consider the BeachNightMarket map regardless of the day of the year because a player could warp from the MermaidHouse to the BeachNightMarket even if there is no sequence of warps from a player's current location to them at this time. So if your brand new map also has warps set up, this mod should be able to check it. If you specifically want to check just your one map, then warp the player there and run "escapemap"

- This mod ignores MineShaft and VolcanoDungeon locations as well as any location not found in Game1.locations (for example AnimalHouse locations). If your map is a custom version of these, try loading it into the game without giving it any special types and then run this mod's command.

- If the mod reports a tile and you cannot figure out how to get to it, try adding the print (or grid) optional argument. If that still doesn't yield insight, it is likely that another loaded map has a warp to a tile next to (or in the vicinity of) the reported tile even if that warp is to an impassable tile on your map, so check warps to your map. It is still possible that the report is a false positive, though.

- Other mods may print warnings when you first use the "escapemap" command. This is a result of how this mod explores locations to do its job well. These warnings (in my experience) only get printed one time and are harmless, so feel free to ignore them. If you like, you can run the "escapemap" command with your chosen arguments a second time to get a response only from this mod.

- If you are not a map maker and you use this mod and find a place where the player can leave the map, please be patient and kind if you choose to report this to the person who made or patched the map. Feel free to direct them to this mod so they can test themselves (they probably know the map and its interactions better and so can use this mod more effectively).

- This mod has no i18n setup and it is not open source. These are limitations of the current nature of this project.

[/size][size=5][b]How does it work?[/b][/size][size=3]

[b]In short:[/b]

It finds tiles on a map where a player can explore based on the forms of travel available to them throughout the currently loaded save file (including walking from the player's current tile) and then it performs a flood fill algorithm based on walkability from those tiles to find out of bounds spots.

[b]In more detail:[/b]

This mod scans through every vanilla form of travel as well as nearly every modded form of travel* to find maps where ConcernedApe or mod makers expect that a player is able to travel to at some point in the course of game play. For good measure, it includes the player's current tile in the currently loaded game because walking is a form of travel that it includes in its check - this allows it to check unreachable maps only if the player is currently standing in that map (e.g. a new map that does not have warps set up). However if a player cannot currently travel to a map, the mod may still scan it if a player in any location in Game1.locations allows the player to travel to this map (e.g. between the mermaid house and beach night market map on a day not during the festival).

In graph theory terms: the mod creates a directed graph in which nodes are tiles used for travel (warps, minecarts, etc.) and directed edges are defined by available forms of travel from one node to the next. Maps are [i]not[/i] nodes. The mod will explore every node of a disconnected directed graph provided the node has any edge pointing to it. (The mod creates a fake edge within the current map to allow it to include the player's current location in its work in case the current map has no other edge pointed to its tiles.)

The resulting scan produces a collection of tiles where a player can arrive to, be they from walking within a map, walking to a neighboring map, taking a mod added minecart, taking the parrot express, etc., and then it processes those further by looking at every tile in the map where a player can walk starting at each of those "arrival tiles." This step of the mod is handled by a flood fill algorithm based on "walkability" in the map. See the section below for how the mod checks if a tile is walkable.

Finally, it checks if a player can walk out of the bounds of the map based on the flood fill scans. Note the "used for travel" portion of the walkable check below - this mod knows about the effects of all kinds of touch actions which means it knows that off map warps also prevent going out of bounds. If your map is missing an off map touch warp, this mod will find it (e.g. in vanilla 1.6.8 the Backwoods and Summit maps, both of which should be fixed in 1.6.9).

*notable exceptions: obelisks added by mods (I can add them, just didn't - let me know if you need them), most travel types added using C#


[/size][size=5][b]How does this mod determine if a tile is walkable?[/b][/size][size=3]

Since this mod's source is not available, here's a mix of C# and pseudocode for that particular check:[/size]

[code]﻿public static bool TestWalkable(GameLocation gameLocation, Vector2 tile, bool showLogMessage = false, bool showHUDMessage = false)
        {
            Vector2 tileCenter = CenterOfTile(tile);
            Rectangle tileRectangle = new Rectangle((int)tileCenter.X - 6, (int)tileCenter.Y - 6, 12, 12);//a rectangle that's smaller than a tile

            if the tile is a touch warp (including an off map touch warp)
                return true;

            if (IsHardCodedImpassableElement(gameLocation, tile))//e.g. Mines boulder, island turtles, etc.
                return false;

            foreach (Building building in gameLocation.buildings)
            {
                if (building.intersects(tileRectangle))
                    return false;
            }

            foreach (LargeTerrainFeature largeTerrainFeature in gameLocation.largeTerrainFeatures)
            {
                if (largeTerrainFeature.getBoundingBox().Contains(tileCenter))
                    return false;
            }

            if (InteriorDoorDictionary.GetDoorTilesFromMapProperty(gameLocation).Contains(tile.ToPoint()))
                return true;

            Tile backTile = gameLocation.map.RequireLayer("Back").Tiles[(int)tile.X, (int)tile.Y];
            Tile buildingsTile = gameLocation.map.RequireLayer("Buildings").Tiles[(int)tile.X, (int)tile.Y];

            if (backTile != null && (backTile.TileIndexProperties.ContainsKey("Passable") || backTile.Properties.ContainsKey("Passable")))
                return false;
            if (buildingsTile != null && !(buildingsTile.TileIndexProperties.ContainsKey("Passable") || buildingsTile.Properties.ContainsKey("Passable")))
                return false;
            
            return true;
        }
[/code]
Note added 2024-10-20: The mod's walkable check (in the above code) considers all trees to be walkable because a player can chop them down. However the mod does not include the fact that trees in town are not able to be chopped down even though they still register as trees - in other words, a few tiles in town (or anywhere that uses the same idea) are treated as walkable when they are not in the normal course of game play.
